messages:
matt: Heads-up — started a quick thread: should routing policy visibility (and editable flags) live inside the role editor or be a separate 'routing' admin page?

sara: I lean separate page. Routing policies touch infra config (regional fallbacks, cost tiers) — not something tenant admins should edit frequently.

lee: Agree with Sara. But we need a clear preview of 'effective routing' on the role side when you grant a user route-level perms. Otherwise they'll think they can route to any variant.

jonah: Can we do both? Keep edit surface in a routing admin, but show a compact read-only summary in the role editor: e.g., routes + max quota visible.

katie: +1 for read-only summary. Also we should hide sensitive knobs (e.g., cost-tier overrides) unless you have "RoutingAdmin" enterprise role. Some customers asked for that separation.

matt: Thinking about telemetry: when we show the summary in role editor, telemetry should track who viewed it (for audits). That helps SRE/infosec.

lee: For audit we already have an event schema, could add `ui.route_summary.view` with fields: user, role_id, tenant_id, route_id. Small payload.

jonah: Quick API sketch — something like:
```json
GET /admin/v1/roles/{role_id}/effective-routes
response: {"routes": [{"id":"route-a","quota_limit":"100k/tok","can_edit":false}]}
```
This keeps edit actions separate.

katie: Edge case: if a tenant admin has permission to edit a route but not to change cost-tier, the UI needs to surface that distinction. Otherwise they'll try to flip a toggle and hit a 403.

matt: UX idea: disable controls with tooltip: "Requires RoutingAdmin or CostOverride flag" + a link to request access. Keeps the editor from being a surprise 403.

rbac-bot: Note: creating separate APIs will require authz checks on both endpoints; role editor summary uses read-only scope `roles:read:routes`.

jonah: Implementation concern: fetch pattern — role editor already loads role + entitlements. Adding route summary might add 2s latency if we fetch full route catalog. Can we only request routes referenced by the role?

lee: Yes, request only referenced routes. Fallback: show placeholders and lazy-load full details on expand.

matt: Ok plan draft: (1) Routing config stays in Routing admin page (editable by RoutingAdmin). (2) Role editor shows read-only summary for referenced routes + disabled controls when lacking flags. (3) Telemetry event `ui.route_summary.view` + `ui.route_action.attempt` on disabled clicks. (4) API endpoint `GET /admin/v1/roles/{role_id}/effective-routes` that returns minimal route info.

sara: Love it. Can we add a short copy in the role editor: "Route-level controls are managed by your Routing Admin" for enterprise orgs? Decreases support tickets.

matt: Good call. I'll pick this up — will draft a small RFC and include the API sketch + telemetry schema. Will also attach a tiny mock for the read-only summary.

katie: Thanks — ping me for the mock review.

matt: pinged. end.
